newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries slightly down after London losses.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries slightly down after London losses.

text.p: Prices of U.S. Treasury securities opened slightly lower Tuesday after slumping somewhat in late London trading as dealers seized the opportunity to take profits.

However, few market participants expect losses of any significant size as sentiment remains buoyed by underlying economic fundamentals: inflation is seen under control and growth is believed to have moderated to sustainable levels.
The Federal Reserve is seen refraining from any tightening of monetary policy and perhaps even changing from a tightening bias.

The only data due this session are the BTM/Schroders report for the week ended July 5 at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT; the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond's regional survey at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT; the Redbook report at 1455 EDT/1855 GMT, and consumer credit for May at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.
"The important story today is going to be dip buying. Every time the market goes down people are going to be kicking themselves," said Patrick Dimick, trader at UBS Securities Inc.
He attributed the late swoon in London to profit-taking but does not expect any radical movement this session.
Given the parabolic run the market has seen in the past three sessions, a correction was inevitable, Dimick said, but underlying sentiment remains very positive.
"We'll be driven by technicals" and could see more mortgage-backed to Treasuries trade, he said.
"There was some choppy selling overseas, but this still looks to be a relatively constructive market," said Jerry Zukowski, economist at PaineWebber.
The market was awaiting the June Producer Price Index, due Friday. The figures, and other numbers scheduled for release next week, are expected to be good.
The Treasury 30-year bond was trading down 7/32 at 100-13/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
At the short end, three-month bills were up one basis point at 4.98 percent, and six-month and year bills were unchanged at 5.08 percent and 5.25 percent, respectively.
Ten-year issues were down 3/32 at 102-18/32, yielding 6.27 percent. Five years were down 2/32 at 100-10/32 to yield 6.18 percent. Two-year notes were down 1/32 at 100-5/32 to yield 5.91 percent.
